Chapter 8: The Law of Sacrifice—Giving Up to Go Up.
Let’s talk about something every real leader faces sooner or later—sacrifice.
If you want to move forward as a leader, you’ll have to let go of something. It might be comfort, convenience, or even a project you really care about. That’s the heart of this principle: to go up, you have to give up.
Now, sacrifice isn’t always dramatic. Sometimes, it’s as simple as staying a little later to help your team through a tough spot. Other times, it means stepping back so someone else can shine, or making a hard decision for the good of the group—even when it’s not the popular choice.
Picture this: a coach who gives up evenings and weekends mentoring young athletes. Instead of enjoying extra free time, they’re out on the field, making sure every player has a shot to succeed. That kind of commitment doesn’t go unnoticed. It builds loyalty, respect, and a culture where everyone wants to give their best.
So, what does sacrifice look like in everyday leadership? Here are a few practical ways it shows up:
First, it’s about taking responsibility for the tough calls, and sometimes shielding your team from extra stress.
Second, it means letting go of control—trusting others to lead, even if that means stepping back yourself.
And third, real leaders invest in the growth of others, sometimes putting their own advancement on hold so the team can move ahead.
But here’s something important to remember: sacrifice isn’t about being a martyr, or ignoring your own needs. It’s a thoughtful choice to put the mission and your people first.
Over time, these acts of service build trust and inspire others to step up too.
So, when you’re faced with a tough choice, ask yourself—what am I willing to give up, so we can go up?
